name: Botch
label: Hydra Head
lede: Four Tacoma kids picked their name out of a dictionary, made two albums that math-metal still measures itself against, and broke up before anyone was watching.

eras.title: Weird kids from Tacoma
eras.text: Four high schoolers start a band in Tacoma with a dictionary for a naming system and a taste for odd time signatures. Seattle's hardcore crews don't quite know what to do with them, and their first records come out on tiny labels.

q: We were viewed as new jacks and weird kids from Tacoma.
years.h: Dave Knudson asks Tim Latona to start a band in the cafeteria
years.p: Guitarist [[Dave Knudson|bf8db0b5-3de5-4a5d-b6e6-392f511736b7]] pitches drummer [[Tim Latona|75ac8921-f30d-4c42-9416-22a5dcd2d46e]] at their Tacoma high school; singer Dave Verellen and bassist [[Brian Cook|e5915350-afd0-405b-a461-f9c9420f9509]] complete Botch, named by opening a dictionary.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, the name came from flipping open a dictionary. Cook has said Knudson lured him in with the promise of recording a Dead Kennedys cover.

All four were still in high school, and Tacoma's hardcore kids were not exactly waiting for them: Cook later recalled the band being seen as 'new jacks' and 'weird kids from Tacoma' by the Seattle scene.

years.h: Faction, the debut 7-inch
years.p: Botch's first record is a seven-inch on World of Hurt and Threshold, and the band's first tour follows in a van driven by Dave Verellen's father, into Canada.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes that the first tour outside Seattle was a Canadian run with Verellen's dad behind the wheel. The band then spent roughly four years as a garage band, releasing demos and EPs before any real label came calling.

years.h: The John Birch Conspiracy Theory EP on Phyte
years.p: The second EP arrives on Phyte, adding more jagged, math-brained hardcore to the band's early catalog.

years.h: The Unifying Themes of Sex, Death and Religion collects the early years
years.p: Excursion Records compiles both EPs plus 'Closure' into one disc, including the band's cover of Carl Orff's 'O Fortuna'. That cover is what caught the ear of [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] at Hydra Head Records.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Turner found the band after praising their take on 'O Fortuna' and signed them. Excursion later put the record back out as Unifying Themes Redux in 2002 with extra tracks from the Nineironspitfire and [[Murder City Devils|32705a3c-54cf-4e48-a3ab-2801157a09dc]] splits; Hydra Head reissued the Redux version in 2006 in orange, not the original blue.

eras.title: Hydra Head and the work lights
eras.text: Signed to Aaron Turner's label, Botch records two albums with Matt Bayles at Studio Litho and turns the live show into a spectacle of its own. They tour with The Dillinger Escape Plan, and Seattle shows get bigger.

years.h: American Nervoso, the Hydra Head debut
years.p: Recorded in March 1998 at Studio Litho in Seattle with [[Matt Bayles|e294077f-71eb-401f-a36a-f2dbcbd75863]], the nine-track album arrives on Hydra Head on May 20.
years.xp: Aaron Turner has said he put six or seven grand into the record. Bayles produced with the band, and the 2007 reissue restored two opening measures of 'Hives' that had been lopped off in the original mastering.

years.cap: Work lamps aimed at the audience
years.h: Halogen work lights point at the crowd, not the band
years.p: On the American Nervoso tour, Botch starts aiming halogen work lamps at the audience, so faces light up and Dave Verellen can watch the room react.
years.xp: Wikipedia quotes Verellen saying the rig let him see people's reactions because their faces were totally illuminated. The first headlining tour behind the album also had The Dillinger Escape Plan and Jesuit on it.

years.h: Rkcndy, a doomed all-ages club, hosts the Romans release show
years.p: Botch plays Seattle's Rkcndy alongside The Blood Brothers, Playing Enemy and Kill Sadie as the club waits for demolition to make way for a hotel.
years.xp: The show came just before the album's release. Louder notes the band was also on the cover of Seattle paper The Rocket around this time, walking away from the camera.

years.h: We Are the Romans, cut in a single week at Litho
years.p: Tracked at Studio Litho with Matt Bayles between June 29 and July 8, 1999, the album's title comes from closer 'Man the Ramparts'.
years.xp: Verellen described the Roman theme as starting from a gladiator-ish feel and turning into commentary on American decline. Cook drew on J.G. Ballard's The Atrocity Exhibition. 'Frequency Ass Bandit' was a last-minute rewrite of 'Frequenting Mass Transit', from an earlier split.

years.big: A hardcore record with the hardcore clichés removed
years.h: No palm-muting, no open-E power chords
years.p: Dave Knudson told Aaron Turner the new record would be heavy and aggressive but avoid the standard hardcore moves.
years.xp: Louder reports Knudson's pitch to Turner was that We Are the Romans would not have any palm-muting or open-E power chords. Cook has pointed to math-rock acts like [[Chavez|c08d2dcd-3c9a-4e5c-b444-c48936de2707]] and [[Don Caballero|b93697af-a318-417a-b16e-a9eb47fbe2f8]] as touchstones, though the band made its own thing out of them.

years.h: Europe and the US with The Dillinger Escape Plan
years.p: Botch tours Europe with Dillinger in 2000 and plays a smaller North American run, with well-attended Seattle shows in early 2000, per Louder.

eras.title: An anthology of dead ends
eras.text: Writer's block, the pressure of following a record everyone loved, and a rift between two of the members. Knudson starts a softer side project, and Botch decides to end it before it goes sour.

years.h: Krazy Fest 4 in Louisville with Coalesce and Converge
years.p: Botch plays the Kentucky festival on a bill with [[Coalesce|3d722ad8-1986-4ce0-bc98-d0864ef625f2]], [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], Poison the Well and Harkonen.

years.h: Dave Knudson starts Minus the Bear on the side
years.p: Knudson forms [[Minus the Bear|c1e98e4a-4628-4c89-a7a6-0e0171600b05]] with Jake Snider, Erin Tate, Matt Bayles and Cory Murchy: gentler, lighter guitar music than Botch.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the softer material Knudson was writing among the reasons Botch came apart. Minus the Bear's Highly Refined Pirates came out on Suicide Squeeze in November 2002.

years.h: Botch decides to break up
years.p: Tim Latona and Dave Knudson, whose friction started during the We Are the Romans sessions, have stopped talking, and the band announces it is done.
years.xp: According to Latona, it was creative differences, not personal ones. Verellen said it was best to break up while they were on top rather than torture themselves. Writer's block and the weight of the last album played a part too.

years.h: An Anthology of Dead Ends, out after the split
years.p: Recorded at Litho in March 2002, the six-song EP came out October 15 on Hydra Head. Matt Bayles called the sessions incredibly tense.
years.xp: Two songs are live, one was an unfinished riff, and the closer 'Afghamistam' leans on quiet vocals, piano and spoken word. Pitchfork gave it 4.5 out of 10; the CD included a video for 'Saint Matthew Returns to the Womb'.
play: Saint Matthew Returns to the Womb

years.h: Last show, the Showbox, with The Blood Brothers
years.p: On June 15, 2002 Botch plays its final show at the Showbox in Seattle with The Blood Brothers, Harkonen and Playing Enemy. Ben Verellen and all of Playing Enemy join for 'Man the Ramparts'.
years.xp: The show was released as 061502 on December 5, 2006 through Hydra Head, a DVD of 14 songs plus an audio CD.

eras.title: The long afterlife
eras.text: Botch stays broken up while its members build other bands, and the two records grow into touchstones. Hydra Head reissues them, then folds, and the rights end up somewhere new.

years.h: Brian Cook and the Verellens: These Arms Are Snakes and Roy
years.p: Cook forms [[These Arms Are Snakes|e95a296e-a34c-4496-9a7c-a95683d487b5]] in Seattle with Steve Snere, and joins Dave and Ben Verellen in the folk-rock band Roy, whose Tacomatose came out in 2003.

years.h: Hydra Head remasters both albums
years.p: American Nervoso is remastered on July 7 and We Are the Romans on September 11, with demos and live tracks on the second disc of the latter.
years.xp: Bayles handled the remastering. In September 2011 a repress of the vinyl reportedly sold through about 450 jackets in under 20 minutes.

years.h: Brian Cook joins Russian Circles
years.p: Cook becomes bassist for [[Russian Circles|cca40a67-e959-46f8-a3f3-8a3f77d2da9e]], and later plays with Aaron Turner in [[Sumac|9b98f3ed-d24a-479e-bd15-97c16de9f13f]].

years.h: Dave Verellen fronts Narrows
years.p: Verellen sings in [[Narrows|3a9bf775-66f1-4299-b062-5cb0585d5672]] with Ryan Frederiksen, releasing a self-titled EP on Deathwish; he also works as a firefighter.

years.h: Sargent House takes over the Botch catalog
years.p: After Hydra Head went out of business in 2020, Sargent House acquires the full Botch catalog in October 2021. Rumors of a reunion spring up; the band denies them.

eras.title: One last trip through
eras.text: A birthday-party surprise, tickets that sold out in 13 seconds, and a tour that was always meant to end. Botch closes the book on the same stage where the first run ended.

years.h: 'One Twenty Two': the first new Botch song in two decades
years.p: Dave Knudson writes a riff during lockdown as a solo idea, asks Dave Verellen to sing, and it becomes Botch's first new song since 2002 as a bonus track on the Sargent House reissue of We Are the Romans.
years.xp: Knudson has said he thought of Verellen because he knew the best hardcore singer ever. Cook said it was not intended to be a Botch song, but with all four of them on it, it felt right. Matt Bayles mixed it.

years.h: Surprise: Botch plays at Matt Bayles's birthday
years.p: On October 15, 2022, twenty years to the day after An Anthology of Dead Ends, Botch plays 'Saint Matthew Returns to the Womb' at Matt Bayles's private birthday party.
years.xp: The clip went viral. A week later the band announced shows; Seattle's two nights in February 2023 sold out in 13 seconds, per The Stranger.

years.h: Reunion shows at Tacoma's Spanish Ballroom and the Showbox
years.p: Botch plays Tacoma on February 17 and Seattle February 24 and 25, then a 14-date US tour from October to December.

years.h: Europe, UK and Australia
years.p: Botch plays a 14-date EU and UK run in March, with three UK dates, and an Australian leg in May 2024.

q: It's been so good to close things off properly.
years.h: Exactly 22 years later, the Showbox again
years.p: Botch's last show is on June 15, 2024 at the Showbox in Seattle, the same date and room as the 2002 finale.
years.xp: Knudson had said there was no more music on the horizon and the reunion would last a very finite time. Verellen told Kerrang it felt good to close things off properly and write the ending they wanted.

years.h: The final show on record
years.p: A live album and film of the June 15, 2024 Showbox show is announced for release on Sargent House on June 27, 2025.
